## Paragraph Flow

- The paper follows a standard IMRaD-style structure (Abstract → Introduction → Related Work → Methodology → Results → Discussion → Conclusion)
- Each section begins with a transition sentence that situates the reader in the argument, not a subsection listing
- Example (Introduction opening): 'Late-life depression is a pressing public health concern...' — places the reader in the clinical context
- Example (Methodology opening): 'We conducted a systematic search of OpenAlex...' — directly states the action taken
- Example (Results opening): 'The PRISMA-style flow of studies through the abstract-level pipeline...' — transitions from method to findings

All transition sentences pass the 'reader knows why they are reading this chapter' test.

## Jargon and Accessibility

- Technical terms (DerSimonian-Laird, Hedges' g, I², tau², Egger's test) are defined on first use
- Acronyms (PRISMA, PICOS, RoB, GRADE, CES-D, HADS, PHQ-9) are expanded
- Statistical methods are described verbally with interpretive thresholds (Cochrane I² thresholds)
